items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Because the composer, I did some work for Marvin Hamlisch.

ctx.x: I think there’s some unsung orchestrators, like when I listen to “West Side Story” and you look like okay who orchestrated this, because it was brilliantly done, at least in my opinion. So I suppose that’s a whole other part of the music business, being an orchestrator.

It really is. There’s an orchestrator named Kim Scharnberg who went to Eastman with Maria I believe. He could tell you some stories. But generally, I forgot the orchestrator for — a major orchestrator for “West Side Story,” anyway, those guys were really the backbone. Because the composer, I did some work for Marvin Hamlisch. And this guy, I mean he had two or three lines that — well anyway the orchestrator would take this jumble and make it into something important. I orchestrated on “A Chorus Line” for part of…
So you based most of your life on the fact that you had this urge, you heard something in your head, you wrote it down and you waited for someone to play it.
